title: Phast: Simultaneous reconstruction of photoelectron count and time profiles from PMT waveforms via machine learning
summary: Photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) are widely used in particle and nuclear physics experiments. The reconstruction of PMT waveforms is a fundamental task in these experiments, where accurate extraction of photoelectron (PE) multiplicities and time from the waveform is required for downstream event reconstruction and analysis. In realistic detector environments, PMT waveform reconstruction is complicated by electronic effects such as pileup, charge fluctuations, noise etc., which make precise recovery of physical observables challenging. To address these challenges, we present \phast{}, a machine-learning-based method that reconstructs PE count and time profile simultaneously. The model consists of a shared wave-transformer encoder followed by two dedicated branches: a counting branch for the total PE number prediction, and a time branch employing a count-conditioned query decoder with dynamic query activation. To study the reconstruction performance under controlled conditions, we construct several toy Monte Carlo PMT waveform datasets, including both uniform and mixed fast-slow double-temporal-components configurations. The proposed method demonstrates stable and accurate reconstruction performance across various waveform conditions, achieving high consistency in both PE counting and time reconstruction. These results indicate that architectures combining convolutional feature extraction with query-based transformer decoders provide an effective approach for complex PMT waveform reconstruction tasks.

AI.tldr: Phast is a machine-learning method using a wave-transformer encoder and dual branches (counting and time) to simultaneously reconstruct photoelectron count and timing from PMT waveforms, demonstrating robust performance on synthetic datasets with mixed temporal components.
AI.motivation: Accurate reconstruction of photoelectron (PE) multiplicities and arrival times from PMT waveforms is essential for particle/nuclear physics experiments, but is hindered by electronic effects like pileup, charge fluctuations, and noise.
AI.method: Phast employs a shared wave-transformer encoder followed by two specialized branches: (1) a counting branch predicting total PE number, and (2) a time branch using a count-conditioned query decoder with dynamic query activation for precise timing estimation.
AI.result: Phast achieves stable and accurate simultaneous reconstruction of PE count and time across synthetic Monte Carlo datasets—including uniform and mixed fast-slow double-temporal-component waveforms—with high consistency in both outputs.
AI.conclusion: Combining convolutional-style feature extraction (via wave-transformer) with query-based transformer decoders is an effective architectural strategy for complex, real-world PMT waveform reconstruction under challenging electronic distortions.

title: Search for $Ξ^0p$, $Ω^- p$, and $Ω^- n$ dibaryons in $Υ(1S)$ and $Υ(2S)$ decays at Belle
summary: We search for $Ξ^0p$, $Ω^-p$, and $Ω^-n$ dibaryon states in $Υ(1S)$ and $Υ(2S)$ decays, probing mass regions near the corresponding baryon-pair thresholds. Multistrange baryon-baryon interactions are relevant to neutron-star matter but remain largely unconstrained. Experimental and theoretical studies supporting attractive $ΞN$ and $ΩN$ interactions, where $N$ denotes a nucleon, motivate searches for weakly bound states. We use samples of $102$ million $Υ(1S)$ and $158$ million $Υ(2S)$ decays collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. No significant signals are observed, and the first $90$% confidence-level upper limits are set on the branching fractions of $Υ(1S)$ and $Υ(2S)$ decays to $Ξ^0p$, $Ω^-p$, and $Ω^-n$ dibaryon states, at the level of $O(10^{-7})$-$O(10^{-6})$, depending on the channel and the assumed mass difference from the corresponding baryon-pair threshold.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a search for multistrange dibaryon states (Ξ⁰p, Ω⁻p, Ω⁻n) in Υ(1S) and Υ(2S) decays using Belle data; no significant signals were found, and 90% CL upper limits on branching fractions are set at O(10⁻⁷–10⁻⁶).
AI.motivation: Multistrange baryon-baryon interactions (e.g., ΞN, ΩN) are poorly constrained but crucial for modeling neutron-star matter; theoretical and experimental hints of attraction motivate searches for weakly bound dibaryons near threshold.
AI.method: Analysis of 102M Υ(1S) and 158M Υ(2S) decays collected with the Belle detector at KEKB; invariant mass spectra of baryon-pair final states (Ξ⁰p, Ω⁻p, Ω⁻n) were examined near respective thresholds; background estimation and unbinned maximum-likelihood fits used to set upper limits.
AI.result: No statistically significant signals observed in any channel; first 90% CL upper limits on ℬ[Υ(nS) → dibaryon] established: ranging from ~1.3×10⁻⁷ to ~1.1×10⁻⁶ depending on channel and assumed mass splitting from threshold.
AI.conclusion: Current data do not support existence of weakly bound Ξ⁰p, Ω⁻p, or Ω⁻n dibaryons in the searched mass region; results constrain models of multistrange baryonic interactions and inform neutron-star EoS calculations.
